newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners still far below Taiwan stock ceiling.

text.p: Foreign investors have remitted US$11.68 billion into Taiwan's stock market, leaving room for US$84.15 billion more before hitting the official ceiling, the central bank said on Friday.
As of April 7, foreign investors may invest up to $95.83 billion in the stock market under rules capping foreign holdings at 25 percent of the bourse's market value, the bank said in a statement.
In September 1996, the bank raised the ceiling to 25 percent from 20 percent and allowed foreign individuals to trade Taiwan stocks.
A central bank official declined to comment whether Taiwan would further ease the ceiling on foreign stock investment in the near future.
"There is plenty of room at the moment," the official told reporters.
Officials have said the government would review the ceiling on foreign stock investment in May.
In March, foreign funds remitted into the stock market totalled US$1.38 billion, up from US$1.31 billion in February, the statement said.
A total of US$725.57 million of such funds flowed out of Taiwan in March, down from February's US$969.75 million.
Aside from direct stock market holdings, the bank has allowed inflow of a total of $1.57 billion for funds raised overseas by local firms through convertible bonds and global depositary receipts.
In this category, foreigners as of April 7 had remitted US$537 million into Taiwan and could send US$1.03 billion more before reaching a legal ceiling, the bank said.
